title: Portrait of a dramatic stellar crib
caption: The Tarantula Nebula and its surroundings, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: 30 Doradus, NGC 2070, NGC 2100, SN 1987A, Tarantula Nebula · constellation Dorado · about 170000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Ranked #37 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: The spidery Tarantula Nebula sits in the upper center of this wide view. A little to the lower right, a web of filaments surrounds the site of the famous supernova SN 1987A, and many other reddish nebulae are scattered across the frame. On the left lies a cluster of young stars called NGC 2100.

The whole scene covers one square degree of sky, a wide area for a detailed telescope image. It places the Tarantula within a busy neighborhood of star formation that also holds young clusters, other glowing clouds and the remains of an exploded star.

The picture was built from observations by Joao Alves, Benoit Vandame and Yuri Beletsky using the Wide Field Imager on the 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla. It is a two-by-two mosaic, combining broad blue and visual filters with narrow filters that capture the glow of hydrogen and of oxygen.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (62.40 x 62.31 arcminutes) and distance (170000 light years), the frame spans roughly 3,100 × 3,100 light-years. Its light set out about 170,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light mosaic from the Wide Field Imager combines B and V broad-band filters with narrow-band H-alpha and oxygen filters. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Long exposures and narrow filters bring out faint glowing gas that would be far too dim, and not so colorful, to the eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: ESO's Advanced Data Products group did the first processing of the data, using the ESO/MVM pipeline.
alt: A wide field with the spidery Tarantula Nebula at upper center, a web of filaments at lower right, several reddish nebulae, and a star cluster on the left.
